Time is pages, not windows — so every quantity has exactly one period and one answer

THE BUG CLASS THIS SCREEN EXISTS TO KILL

Seven overlapping windows, four answers

Trailing windows all ending "now" made one question yield several answers, and made This month identical to 3 months. Pages are calendar-aligned and never overlap, so a number belongs to exactly one period.

The consequence that shapes every frame here: the headline, every card and the record list ride the same page and move together. The pager cannot be a control that re-filters cards in place — that would put two periods on one screen again.

DRAWN AS STAT TABLES FIRST — YOUR CALL, AND §D4'S OWN ESCAPE HATCH

Charts are not installed, and these pages do not wait for them

"A chart that cannot earn a headline and a sentence is a stat table instead." Every card below carries its headline, its sentence and its period receipt — so Insights ships its information architecture, its pager and its honesty rules before a single canvas exists.

Marks arrive later without an IA change. Sheet 02 §08 holds the target grammar for each card.

FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS THIS SHEET TOUCHES · ALL TAKEN AT THEIR RECOMMENDATION
#2 Fuel headline period — page-scoped mean, keeping inv.4's ≤5 window as "your usual". Both are drawn, and on this page they differ.
#3 By-week bucketing — day-of-month blocks, so buckets telescope exactly to the month total.
#11 The lens-picker title — drawn with no title. Four rows say what they are, and "lens" never becomes user-facing vocabulary.
Default page size — Month, landing on today's partial page. Sometimes sparse, and July is drawn sparse rather than flattered.

Four bars, four domain hues, summing to the headline exactly — 289,00 + 98,20 + 96,50 + 4,20 = 487,90 €. Rows name the plan type, never the brand. Records are amount-descending because this card is evidence for where it went; recency would duplicate History's ordering. Six is the cap and July has six, so no N more link appears.

Two honest gaps in one card. 15–21 July reads — because nothing was spent; 29–31 July reads not yet because today is the 28th. A block that has not happened and a block that cost nothing are different facts, and a single 0,00 € would flatten both.

This is §16 #2 drawn, not described. The headline is the page-scoped mean — 7,1 over July's two measured fills — while your usual is inv.4's ≤5-value window at 6,85. They differ, so the page shows both and labels which is which. A page that quietly borrowed the trailing figure would be answering a question the pager did not ask.

Below three measured fills the PER FILL chart is refused, not faked — a two-point trend is not a trend. The dots teach what would fix it, and they are the one place progress dots are allowed: they instruct, they do not reward.

The litres total is the honesty test

July's three fills carry 72,54 L — all three recorded litres, so all three are in the total. What the 24 July fill lacks is an odometer, and that is a different loss: it costs the economy interval, not the litres. Litres bought in July belong to July. Only if a fill had recorded no litres at all would the total disappear — a sum that would lie is withheld, never shown as zero and never as ≈.

All-cars fuel shows tiles, never a blend

Blending economy across cars is physically meaningless, so it is a constitutional refusal — not a display preference. Scope set to Both replaces the whole lens body with one tile per car.

Golf GTI
7,1 L/100km
steady · 3 fills
Ibiza
≈5,4 L/100km

The Ibiza's ≈ is doing real work: only half its fills were full, so its figure is an estimate and says so on the tile itself.

A page with no records refuses its own headline

An empty Cost page does not read 0,00 € — that is a lie by omission, since the user cannot tell "spent nothing" from "logged nothing". It reads "Nothing logged in June." plus one sentence, and renders no cards at all.

What never enters a Cost total

A note (not money). A trip (its ≈costs are a share of money already counted, and it belongs to Distance). A purchase price — a fact, not a charge, so never a bar and never in the total; it lives on Ownership. And a plan's deposit never appears as a monthly charge.

The gauge is pinned, and it sits above the divider on purpose. A lease cycle anchors to the plan's start day-of-month, so it is not a calendar page and must not pretend to be one — it carries its own dates and does not move when the pager does. Its denominator is the pooled budget: a car with 260 km banked is not over until it passes 1.760.

Arithmetic, checked: the two measured blocks sum to 412 km (266 + 146), matching the headline; 412 ÷ 28 = 14,71 km/day; the projection runs 78 days past the 12 July reading at that pace — 91.240 + 1.148 ≈ 92.388 by 28 September. The 232 km trip is a subset of the 412, never added to it.

The pager is gone — not disabled, gone. Ownership is timeless; "since 2014" is not a page, so there is no period label, no chevrons and no TODAY. This is also the lens that needs no canvas at all: a ledger card and a rate table lose nothing, which makes it the cheapest real lens to build first.

The purchase price sits above the ledger line, not in it. 2.145,80 + 890,30 + 156,40 = 3.192,50 € — the 9.200,00 € is deliberately not added, because a fact is not a charge. An owned car has no plan charges, so that row is a dash rather than a hidden row: showing the empty category is what proves the total is complete.

Sizes are named with their resolution, so you know what the bars will be before committing. That is why grain is not a separate control.

Over-cap says the same thing the garage chip says

CAP CYCLE · 23 JUL – 22 AUG
1.840 / 1.760 km
1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June.
80 km over your pooled budget.
At your pace, ≈2.035 km by 22 August.

Fills attention, counts the overage in text, keeps the pace line present tense. Never hidden, never red, nothing flashes — being over a mileage cap is a fact about a contract, not an error the user made.

Interpolation, and why sparse trails draw low even bars

Buckets interpolate the trail linearly between readings, so a year-wide gap spreads across the months it covers instead of spiking in the month the next reading lands. Two readings a year apart draw twelve small bars, not one tall one — that is correct, and it needs no caption. Buckets still telescope exactly to last − first.

Page size keeps your place

July (month) → 2026 (year) → back to Month lands on July again. Year → Month drills into that year, never into today. A year page also drops the record list entirely — wider pages hand the list to History, because a year of rows is History's job.

Sheet 10 of batch 2. Next: 11 the record pages · 12 reminders and the vault · 13 onboarding. The carousel itself is an implementation note, not a design one — three interval-keyed pages, re-keyed on settle, with the horizontal pan owning the page and the vertical pan owning the scroll.
